q: The general electronic configuration of d-block (transition) elements is:
why: Transition elements have the general configuration (n-1)d^(1-10) ns^(0-2).

q: The correct electronic configuration of chromium (Z=24), showing extra stability of half-filled orbitals, is:
why: Cr has configuration 3d5 4s1 instead of the expected 3d4 4s2, due to extra stability of a half-filled d-subshell.

q: Among the first-row transition metals, which element shows the widest range of oxidation states (+2 to +7)?
why: Manganese shows oxidation states from +2 to +7, the widest range among 3d transition metals, due to its d5 configuration at +2.

q: The common +2 oxidation state of most 3d transition metals arises from the loss of:
why: The +2 state is commonly achieved by loss of the two 4s electrons, since 4s is lost before 3d on ionisation.

q: The magnetic moment formula relating the number of unpaired electrons (n) to magnetic moment (mu) in Bohr magnetons is:
why: Magnetic moment mu = sqrt(n(n+2)) Bohr magneton, where n is the number of unpaired electrons.

q: Ti3+ ion has one unpaired electron (3d1). Its magnetic moment is approximately:
why: mu = sqrt(n(n+2)) = sqrt(1x3) = sqrt(3) ≈ 1.73 BM for one unpaired electron.

q: Zn2+ ion (d10 configuration) is colourless and diamagnetic because:
o: It has unpaired electrons causing colour
It has no unpaired electrons, so no d-d transition is possible
why: With a fully filled d10 configuration, no d-d transition can occur, making the ion colourless and diamagnetic (no unpaired electrons).

q: In the Contact process, V2O5 acts as a catalyst for converting SO2 to SO3 by:
o: Cycling between V2O5 and V2O4 via redox with SO2 and O2
Acting only as a physical adsorbent with no chemical change
why: V2O5 is reduced by SO2 to V2O4, then reoxidised by O2 back to V2O5, repeatedly converting SO2 to SO3.

q: Lanthanoid contraction occurs mainly due to:
o: Poor shielding by 4f electrons, increasing effective nuclear charge
Addition of electrons to the 5d orbitals
Decrease in nuclear charge across the series
why: Poor shielding by 4f electrons increases effective nuclear charge, pulling the outer shell inward and causing lanthanoid contraction.

q: As a result of lanthanoid contraction, which pair of elements have almost identical atomic radii, making separation difficult?
why: Lanthanoid contraction causes Zr and Hf to have nearly identical radii, making their chemical separation very difficult.
